name: Maryland veterans: accredited claims help
organization: Maryland Department of Veterans and Military Families, Service and Benefits Program
description: Free help from VA-accredited benefits specialists with VA claims, applications and appeals for veterans, dependents and survivors.
next_step: Choose your county for its service office, or call the statewide service line at 800-446-4926 ext. 6450. Offices are by appointment only.
constraints: Offices are open Monday–Friday, 8:00 a.m.–4:00 p.m., by appointment only; call the office first.

name: Maryland Access Point (Aging and Disability Resource Center)
description: Maryland’s statewide entry point to long-term services and supports for older adults and people with disabilities: information, referral and options counseling through local Maryland Access Point offices, led mainly by Area Agencies on Aging with Centers for Independent Living. Military service is not required.
next_step: Call 1-844-627-5465 (1-844-MAP-LINK) or dial 211 and ask for Maryland Access Point. Choose a county above for the direct number of its Area Agency on Aging.
constraints: Each program has its own eligibility and waitlist.

name: Medicare counseling (SHIP) for Maryland
organization: Maryland Department of Aging, Senior Health Insurance Assistance Program (SHIP)
description: Free Medicare counseling from the Senior Health Insurance Assistance Program. Each Area Agency on Aging has a SHIP coordinator and trained volunteers who help with plan enrollment and Extra Help applications.
next_step: Call 800-243-3425 and ask for Medicare counseling (SHIP), or ask your Area Agency on Aging for its SHIP counselor.

name: Maryland Long-Term Care Ombudsman Program
organization: Office of the State Long-Term Care Ombudsman, Maryland Department of Aging
description: Statewide advocacy for residents of nursing homes and assisted living, delivered through the State office and 19 local ombudsman programs located at Area Agencies on Aging.
next_step: Choose your county for its local ombudsman, or call the Maryland Department of Aging at 800-243-3425 and ask for the ombudsman program. To report suspected abuse, neglect or exploitation of an adult, call Adult Protective Services at 800-332-6347. For immediate danger, call 911.
constraints: The ombudsman acts with the resident’s permission and is not a licensing or enforcement agency.

name: Maryland Legal Aid
description: Free civil legal help for people with low income, including a statewide telephone hotline for low-income veterans. Not criminal defense.
next_step: Call central intake at 888-465-2468 and say if you are a veteran. Veterans can also call the Joining Forces hotline at 443-863-4040.
constraints: Applicants are screened; income, case type and capacity limits apply. Criminal, personal injury and traffic matters are not accepted.
The Joining Forces hotline hours listed in a bar-association directory are Tuesdays 3:00–7:00 p.m. and Thursdays 9:30 a.m.–1:30 p.m.; hours can change.

name: VA medical centers serving Maryland
description: VA Maryland Health Care System: Baltimore VA Medical Center (410-605-7000), Perry Point VA Medical Center (410-642-2411) and the Loch Raven campus. The state department lists the Washington DC VA Medical Center (202-745-8000) for Montgomery and Prince George’s Counties and Southern Maryland, and the Martinsburg VA Medical Center in West Virginia (304-263-0811) for Western Maryland. Community clinics are listed in VA’s facility locator.
next_step: Use VA’s facility locator with your ZIP code to find the closest clinic and its medical center. Not enrolled yet? Ask a benefits specialist at your service office for help applying.
constraints: The state’s page names regions rather than counties, so this card does not assign counties. Your VA care team may be at a different clinic or system; follow what VA tells you.

next_step: Call SSVF intake with your county and housing situation: whether you are homeless now or at risk of losing housing, and who lives with you. A second intake number is listed: 301-863-7361.
constraints: Serves only the areas listed; check that yours is included. Veteran-household, income and housing-status screening applies.
County and intake details come from VA’s FY26 SSVF provider intake list; confirm current service when calling.
